quote: You do not have to be good.
source: Mary Oliver, Wild Geese, the opening line, Dream Work (Atlantic Monthly Press, 1986)

evidence.where: The poem is under copyright and no full text was opened from a rights holder. Several independent sources that print the poem or its opening give the same first line and the same first two lines, You do not have to be good followed by You do not have to walk on your knees, and all of them place the poem in Dream Work of 1986. The book is Mary Oliver's fourth collection, published by Atlantic Monthly Press in New York in 1986; later printings carry the Grove Press and Atlantic Monthly Press imprint together, which is why some citations name Grove.

reason: A famous opening line, six words, correctly attributed to the right poem and the right book, with its full stop as printed. One line of a copyrighted poem is a short quotation with attribution. Not shipped, no near match, Oliver at zero of three, not banned, not on the misattribution list.
